First release of Sable Monitor, a real-time monitoring and diagnostics tool
for a single Linux machine.

It reads the kernel's own interfaces, keeps a bounded history in a local
SQLite database, raises alerts against thresholds you set, and serves all of
it to a dashboard bound to the loopback address. There are no runtime
dependencies: storage is Node's built-in SQLite, the server is `node:http`,
and the dashboard is plain ES modules with hand-drawn SVG charts.

## What it collects

- **CPU** from `/proc/stat`: overall and per-core utilisation, load
  averages, logical CPU count, model and current frequency where the kernel
  publishes them, I/O wait and steal time.
- **Memory** from `/proc/meminfo`, using `MemAvailable` so that reclaimable
  page cache is not counted as used, plus swap.
- **Disk**: capacity per mounted filesystem through `statfs`, and read and
  write throughput and busy time per block device from `/proc/diskstats`.
- **Network** from `/proc/net/dev` with link state from `/sys/class/net`.
- **Processes** from `/proc/<pid>/stat`, with search, sorting and filtering.

## Honest measurement

A utilisation or a throughput is the difference between two readings, so the
first sample has none and reports them as unavailable rather than as zero. A
counter that went backwards is a reset, not a spike. An interface that has
just appeared, a CPU that was hot-plugged and a reused PID are each reported
as unmeasured until there is a second reading to compare with. A period when
the agent was not running stays a gap in the chart; nothing is interpolated
or back-filled.

## Alerting

Five rules — high CPU, high memory, low disk space on a writable
filesystem, high sustained load relative to the logical CPU count, and stale
agent data — each with a configurable threshold, an evaluation window,
hysteresis and a cooldown. Alerts are written to the local database and
shown on the dashboard. Nothing is sent anywhere: there is no email, SMS or
webhook integration, by design.

## Security

- Bound to `127.0.0.1` by default. No port is opened, no service is
  installed and no firewall rule is changed.
- `Host` and `Origin` are validated on every request, which is what stops a
  web page — or a hostile name that resolves to `127.0.0.1` — reading the
  API. Binding to loopback is not treated as a security model on its own.
- Only `GET` and `HEAD` exist, so there is no state-changing request to
  forge.
- Process command lines, environments, working directories, open file
  descriptors and memory maps are never read, so a credential passed as an
  argument cannot leak through the dashboard.
- The database and its directory are created with owner-only permissions.
- Binding off loopback requires both an explicit `allowRemote` setting and a
  bearer token of at least sixteen characters, and is refused otherwise. An
  SSH tunnel or a private network is the documented way to reach the
  dashboard remotely.

## Requirements

Linux, and Node.js 24 or later — `node:sqlite` is available without a flag
from 24. CI runs 24 and 26. Root is not required and not recommended.

## Install

Distribution is through GitHub only; this is not published to npm.

```sh
base=https://github.com/sablectl/sable-monitor/releases/download/v1.0.0
curl -fsSLO "$base/sable-monitor-v1.0.0.tar.gz"
curl -fsSLO "$base/sable-monitor-v1.0.0.tar.gz.sha256"
sha256sum -c sable-monitor-v1.0.0.tar.gz.sha256
tar -xzf sable-monitor-v1.0.0.tar.gz
cd sable-monitor-v1.0.0
node dist/bin/sable-monitor.js start
```

Nothing needs to be installed from the tarball before it will run. Open
<http://127.0.0.1:7878>, and press Ctrl-C to stop.

## Measured cost

From `npm run bench` on one laptop — Node v26.3.1, linux-x64, an Intel Core
i7-8750H with 12 logical CPUs and 467 running processes. Measurements from
one machine, not guarantees: 5.05 ms mean per sample, 5.11 ms of CPU per
sample, about 0.51% of one core at a one-second interval, 87.92 MiB
resident, 184.3 bytes per stored sample — roughly 53 MiB for seven days at
the two-second default — and 70.64 ms to list 467 processes.

## Known limitations

`USER_HZ` is assumed to be 100 and the page size 4096 bytes, so per-process
CPU and resident memory are wrong on a kernel built differently. Disk
throughput is per block device while capacity is per filesystem, and the two
cannot be added. Network latency and packet loss are not measured. There is
no container or cgroup-aware accounting, no temperature, fan, SMART or GPU
metrics, and no multi-host aggregation. The full list is in
[docs/known-limitations.md](https://github.com/sablectl/sable-monitor/blob/main/docs/known-limitations.md).
